title: Every Pure Nash Equilibrium of Round-Robin with at Most $2n+1$ Goods Is Envy-Free up to One Good
abstract: In the fair division of indivisible goods under additive valuations, the Round-Robin mechanism guarantees envy-freeness up to one good (EF1) when agents act truthfully. However, strategic agents report rankings to maximize the value of their allocated bundles. In arXiv:2610.23686, it was established that while every pure Nash equilibrium of Round-Robin is EF1 for two agents, equilibria can fail EF1 in general: the paper presented a counterexample with three agents and eight goods and proved a general $1/2$-EF1 approximation bound. The counterexample uses $m = 2n + 2$ goods; how few goods guarantee EF1 for every number of agents is not addressed there. We prove that for any number of agents $n \ge 1$ and any number of goods $m \le 2n + 1$, every pure Nash equilibrium of Round-Robin under nonnegative additive valuations is EF1. The proof decomposes the analysis by turn counts: when $m \le 2n$, every agent picks at most twice, and equilibrium conditions prevent envy exceeding one good; when $m = 2n + 1$, only agent $0$ receives three items while all other agents receive at most two, and a valuation-free deviation argument shows that every other agent is EF1 towards agent $0$ once agent $0$'s first pick is removed. For three agents the bound is tight: the paper's eight-good counterexample is the smallest possible. These results are formalized and verified in Lean 4.
introduction:
The problem of allocating indivisible goods fairly among agents with additive valuations is a foundational topic in social choice and algorithmic game theory. Among the mechanisms designed for this purpose, the Round-Robin protocol is widely studied due to its operational simplicity and strong fairness properties under truthful behavior. In a Round-Robin protocol, agents take turns in cyclic order—agent $0$, then agent $1$, up through agent $n-1$, repeating cyclically—each picking their most preferred available good from a common pool of $m$ items. A well-known classic property of Round-Robin is that when agents report their true valuations and pick myopically, the resulting allocation is guaranteed to be envy-free up to one good (EF1): no agent envies another agent's bundle once some item is removed from the envied bundle.

In real-world decentralized settings, however, agents cannot generally be assumed to act truthfully. When agents know each other's preferences, they may report strategic rankings over the goods rather than their truthful ordinal preferences. A reported strict ranking profile determines the picking sequence outcome: each agent, upon their turn, is allocated their highest-ranked good among those remaining. This induces a normal-form game, the picking-sequence game, in which an agent's strategy is their reported permutation of the items. A profile of reported rankings forms a pure Nash equilibrium (PNE) if no agent can obtain a bundle of strictly greater true additive value by unilaterally deviating to a different reported ranking.

The question of whether strategic behavior preserves the fairness guarantees of Round-Robin was investigated in arXiv:2610.23686. That paper showed that strategic interactions can indeed degrade fairness. While the paper proved that for $n = 2$ agents, every pure Nash equilibrium of Round-Robin produces an allocation that is EF1, the same guarantee does not extend unconditionally to three or more agents. Specifically, arXiv:2610.23686 presented an explicit counterexample in Proposition 1 with $n = 3$ agents and $m = 8$ goods where a pure Nash equilibrium fails to be EF1. On the positive side, arXiv:2610.23686 established that every pure Nash equilibrium of Round-Robin satisfies a $1/2$-EF1 approximation bound for any number of agents and goods.

The counterexample of arXiv:2610.23686 uses $8$ goods for $3$ agents, that is, $m = 2n + 2$ for $n = 3$. This raises a natural question about the role of the number of goods: for $n$ agents, up to how many goods is every pure Nash equilibrium of Round-Robin guaranteed to be EF1? When $m \le n$ every agent picks at most once and EF1 is immediate; the question is what happens once agents pick several times.

In this post we prove, with a Lean 4 formalization, that for every $n \ge 1$ and every $m \le 2n + 1$, every pure Nash equilibrium of Round-Robin under nonnegative additive valuations is EF1 (`round_robin_pne_ef1_of_card_le_two_mul_add_one`). This is a positive guarantee for an infinite family of instances, covering any number of agents.

For $n = 3$ the bound is tight: with $7$ goods every equilibrium is EF1, while the paper's instance with $8$ goods has a non-EF1 equilibrium. So the $8$-good counterexample of arXiv:2610.23686 is the smallest possible for three agents. Whether $2n + 2$ goods suffice to break EF1 for every $n \ge 4$ is not proved here and remains open.
result:
The primary result formalized in Lean 4 is that every pure Nash equilibrium of Round-Robin is EF1 whenever the number of items does not exceed $2n + 1$.

Theorem (`round_robin_pne_ef1_of_card_le_two_mul_add_one`). Let $n, m \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n \ge 1$ and $m \le 2n + 1$. Let $w : \text{Fin } n \to \text{Fin } m \to \mathbb{R}$ be a weight matrix satisfying $w(i, g) \ge 0$ for all $i \in \text{Fin } n$ and $g \in \text{Fin } m$, inducing the additive valuation $v = \text{toValuation}(\langle w \rangle)$. Let $\text{rank} : \text{Fin } n \to (\text{Fin } m \simeq \text{Fin } m)$ be a profile of reported rankings that forms a pure Nash equilibrium of the picking-sequence game for the Round-Robin sequence of length $m$:
$$
\text{is\_picking\_sequence\_pne } v \ (\text{round\_robin\_sequence } n \ m) \ \text{rank}.
$$
Then the allocation resulting from the picking sequence is envy-free up to one good:
$$
\text{SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.IsEF1 } v \ (\text{picking\_sequence\_outcome } (\text{round\_robin\_sequence } n \ m) \ \text{rank}).
$$

In Lean, `round_robin_pne_ef1_of_card_le_two_mul_add_one` universally quantifies over natural numbers $n$ and $m$ with typeclass instance asserting non-zero $n$, an inequality hypothesis $m \le 2n + 1$, an item weight matrix $w$ with nonnegativity hypothesis, a reported ranking permutation profile, and a pure Nash equilibrium hypothesis, concluding that the picking sequence outcome satisfies `SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.IsEF1`.

Further results in the formal development provide additional insight into the structure of equilibria and the sharpness of this bound:

- `round_robin_pne_ef1_of_card_le_two_mul`: Proves that when $m \le 2n$, every pure Nash equilibrium of Round-Robin is EF1 under nonnegative additive valuations. In this regime, every agent appears at most twice in the picking sequence.
- `round_robin_pne_envy_zero_ef1_of_two_mul_add_one`: Establishes that when $m = 2n + 1$, in every pure Nash equilibrium, every agent $i \ne 0$ is EF1 towards agent $0$. Here, agent $0$ is the unique agent who receives three goods, while all other agents receive at most two.
- `round_robin_pne_ef1_pair_of_count_le_two`: Demonstrates that in any pure Nash equilibrium of Round-Robin, an agent $i$ is EF1 towards any agent $j$ who appears at most twice in the sequence.
- `round_robin_three_agents_seven_goods_pne_ef1`: Proves that for $n = 3$ agents and $m = 7$ goods, every pure Nash equilibrium of Round-Robin is EF1. This shows that the $8$-good counterexample of arXiv:2610.23686 is minimal: seven goods are never sufficient to break EF1.
proof:
We now present the proof of `round_robin_pne_ef1_of_card_le_two_mul_add_one` as formalized in Lean.

Overview of the Proof:

We begin with an overview of the proof idea, then state the lemmas on which it rests, and finally combine them to establish the theorem. The analysis splits into two cases depending on the number of items $m$.

In the case where $m \le 2n$, the total number of items is at most twice the number of agents. In the Round-Robin sequence, each agent takes turns at most two times. When an agent picks at most two items, equilibrium incentives prevent any other agent from envying them by more than one good. This case is resolved by `round_robin_pne_ef1_of_card_le_two_mul`.

In the case where $m = 2n + 1$, exactly one agent—agent $0$—picks three items (at turns $0$, $n$, and $2n$). Every other agent $j \in \{1, \dots, n-1\}$ picks at most two items (specifically at turns $j$ and $n + j$). To verify EF1 for the entire allocation, we consider any pair of distinct agents $i$ and $j$:

- If the envied agent $j$ satisfies $j \ne 0$, then $j$ picks at most twice in the sequence. By `round_robin_pne_ef1_pair_of_count_le_two`, agent $i$ does not envy $j$ by more than one good.
- If the envied agent $j$ is agent $0$ ($j = 0$), then $j$ picks three items. However, because $i \ne j$, we have $i \ne 0$. The specialized lemma `round_robin_pne_envy_zero_ef1_of_two_mul_add_one` establishes that any agent $i \ne 0$ is EF1 towards agent $0$.

Combining these cases covers all possible pairs and establishes EF1 for the full allocation.

We now state the supporting lemmas established in the formalization and used in the main theorem.

Lemma 1 (`round_robin_pne_ef1_of_card_le_two_mul`).
Let $n, m \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n \ge 1$ and $m \le 2n$. Let $w : \text{Fin } n \to \text{Fin } m \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy $w(i, g) \ge 0$ for all $i, g$, and let $\text{rank}$ be a pure Nash equilibrium of Round-Robin under the additive valuation induced by $w$. Then the allocation returned by `picking_sequence_outcome` on `round_robin_sequence` is EF1.

Role in Lean: This lemma handles the subcase where $m \le 2n$. When each agent appears at most twice in the sequence, no agent can receive three or more items. If agent $i$ envied agent $j$ after removing any single item from $A_j$, agent $j$ must hold two items $\{g_1, g_2\}$ such that $v_i(\{g_1\}) > v_i(A_i)$ and $v_i(\{g_2\}) > v_i(A_i)$. However, the picking mechanism allows agent $i$ to secure at least one of these high-value items during their own turn if they deviate, contradicting the equilibrium hypothesis `is_picking_sequence_pne`.

Lemma 2 (`round_robin_sequence_count_le_two_of_ne_zero`).
Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n \ge 1$. In the Round-Robin sequence of length $2n + 1$ with $n$ agents, every agent $j$ with $j \ne 0$ appears at most twice:
$$
(\text{round\_robin\_sequence } n \ (2n + 1)).\text{count } j \le 2.
$$

Proof in Lean: The sequence consists of indices $t \in \{0, 1, \dots, 2n\}$, where turn $t$ is allocated to agent $t \pmod n$. Agent $0$ receives turns $t \in \{0, n, 2n\}$, totaling $3$ turns. For any agent $j \in \{1, \dots, n-1\}$, the turns assigned to $j$ are the values $t \in \{0, \dots, 2n\}$ such that $t \equiv j \pmod n$. These are exactly $t = j$ and $t = n + j$. The next potential turn would be $2n + j$; however, since $j \ge 1$, we have $2n + j \ge 2n + 1$, which exceeds the sequence length $m = 2n + 1$. Thus, agent $j$ appears exactly twice, which is bounded by $2$.

Lemma 3 (`round_robin_pne_ef1_pair_of_count_le_two`).
Let $n, m \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n \ge 1$. Let $w$ define nonnegative additive valuations, and let $\text{rank}$ be a pure Nash equilibrium of Round-Robin. For any distinct agents $i, j$, if agent $j$ appears at most twice in the picking sequence,
$$
(\text{round\_robin\_sequence } n \ m).\text{count } j \le 2,
$$
and $A_j$ is nonempty, then agent $i$ is EF1 towards agent $j$:
$$
\exists g \in A_j, \ v_i(A_j \setminus \{g\}) \le v_i(A_i).
$$

Proof in Lean: Since $j$ appears at most twice in the sequence, the bundle $A_j$ contains at most two items: $|A_j| \le 2$. If $|A_j| = 1$, let $A_j = \{g\}$. Removing $g$ leaves the empty set $A_j \setminus \{g\} = \emptyset$. Under nonnegative weights ($w \ge 0$), $v_i(\emptyset) = 0 \le v_i(A_i)$, satisfying the EF1 condition immediately. If $|A_j| = 2$, let $A_j = \{g_1, g_2\}$. Without loss of generality, assume $w(i, g_1) \ge w(i, g_2)$. Choosing $g = g_1$ to remove, we have $A_j \setminus \{g_1\} = \{g_2\}$, and the EF1 condition requires $v_i(\{g_2\}) \le v_i(A_i)$. If this condition failed, then $w(i, g_2) > v_i(A_i)$ and consequently $w(i, g_1) \ge w(i, g_2) > v_i(A_i)$. This would mean both goods in $A_j$ individually yield strictly greater value to agent $i$ than the entirety of agent $i$'s equilibrium bundle $A_i$. Under the picking-sequence mechanism, at least one of these two goods was available at one of agent $i$'s picking turns. Agent $i$ could unilaterally alter their reported ranking to place that good at the top of their ranking, securing an item worth strictly more than $v_i(A_i)$, thereby strictly improving their total bundle value. This contradicts the pure Nash equilibrium condition `is_picking_sequence_pne`. Hence, $v_i(\{g_2\}) \le v_i(A_i)$, proving the pair $(i, j)$ is EF1.

Lemma 4 (`round_robin_pne_envy_zero_ef1_of_two_mul_add_one`).
Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n \ge 1$. In the Round-Robin sequence with $n$ agents and $2n + 1$ goods, under nonnegative additive valuations, in every pure Nash equilibrium $\text{rank}$, every agent $i \ne 0$ is EF1 towards agent $0$:
$$
\exists g \in A_0, \ v_i(A_0 \setminus \{g\}) \le v_i(A_i),
$$
where $A_k = \text{picking\_sequence\_outcome } (\text{round\_robin\_sequence } n \ (2n+1)) \ \text{rank } k$.

Proof in Lean: When $m = 2n + 1$, agent $0$ picks at turns $0$, $n$ and $2n$; call its picks $a_1$, $a_2$, $a_3$, where $a_1$ is the top good of its report. Agent $i \ne 0$ picks at turns $i$ and $n + i$ and receives $A_i = \{b_1, b_2\}$; note $0 < i < n < n + i < 2n$. The good removed from $A_0$ is always $a_1$, so the claim is $w(i, a_2) + w(i, a_3) \le v_i(A_i)$.

The proof first establishes a purely combinatorial fact about the mechanism, independent of valuations: for any reports, either (a) some report $r$ of agent $i$ alone gives agent $i$ a bundle containing both $a_2$ and $a_3$, or (b) two reports $r_1$, $r_2$ of agent $i$ give bundles $D_1$, $D_2$ that together cover $A_i$ and $\{a_2, a_3\}$ with multiplicity: every good is counted in $D_1$ and $D_2$ at least as often as in $A_i$ and $\{a_2, a_3\}$. This is shown by tracing the run of the mechanism through the window of turns between agent $i$'s first pick and agent $0$'s last pick, comparing which goods remain available when agent $i$ takes $a_2$ or $a_3$ early.

The equilibrium condition then finishes the argument. In case (a), $w(i, a_2) + w(i, a_3) \le v_i(\text{bundle under } r) \le v_i(A_i)$, using nonnegative weights and that $r$ is not a profitable deviation. In case (b), the covering gives $v_i(A_i) + w(i, a_2) + w(i, a_3) \le v_i(D_1) + v_i(D_2) \le 2 v_i(A_i)$, again by nonnegativity and the equilibrium condition applied to $r_1$ and $r_2$, so $w(i, a_2) + w(i, a_3) \le v_i(A_i)$.

Combining the Lemmas to Prove the Main Theorem:

We now trace the Lean proof of `round_robin_pne_ef1_of_card_le_two_mul_add_one`:

The proof begins by branching on the inequality $m \le 2n$. In the branch where $m \le 2n$ holds, the proof directly applies `round_robin_pne_ef1_of_card_le_two_mul`, which immediately closes the goal.

In the branch where $m \le 2n$ does not hold, we have $m > 2n$. Combined with the hypothesis $m \le 2n + 1$, Lean's arithmetic tactics establish the exact equality $m = 2n + 1$. The proof substitutes $m$ with $2n + 1$.

To prove `SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.IsEF1`, the proof introduces arbitrary agents $i, j$, the distinctness hypothesis $i \ne j$, and the hypothesis that $A_j$ is nonempty.

The proof then branches on whether $j = 0$. When $j = 0$, substituting $j = 0$ leaves the goal of showing that agent $i$ is EF1 towards agent $0$. Since $i \ne j$ and $j = 0$, we have $i \ne 0$. The proof invokes Lemma 4, `round_robin_pne_envy_zero_ef1_of_two_mul_add_one`, which provides the required item $g \in A_0$. When $j \ne 0$, agent $j$ is not agent $0$. The proof applies Lemma 2, `round_robin_sequence_count_le_two_of_ne_zero`, which confirms that agent $j$ appears at most twice in the sequence. With this count bound and the nonemptiness hypothesis, the proof calls Lemma 3, `round_robin_pne_ef1_pair_of_count_le_two`, which provides the required item $g \in A_j$.

Since both subcases provide an item whose removal eliminates envy, the allocation satisfies the EF1 condition. The Lean proof is complete and fully verified.
discussion:
The result `round_robin_pne_ef1_of_card_le_two_mul_add_one` gives a positive guarantee for the fairness of strategic Round-Robin: every pure Nash equilibrium is EF1 as long as the number of goods satisfies $m \le 2n + 1$. This extends the two-agent EF1 theorem of arXiv:2610.23686, for any number of agents, to the regime where each agent receives at most two goods except agent $0$, who receives three.

For comparison, arXiv:2610.23686 shows for more than two agents that every pure Nash equilibrium is $1/2$-EF1, that exact EF1 can fail (Proposition 1, with $n = 3$ agents and $m = 8$ goods), and that no factor above $2/3$ can be guaranteed, by a family with a growing number of agents and goods.

For $n = 3$, `round_robin_three_agents_seven_goods_pne_ef1` (the case $n = 3$ of the main theorem) shows that every pure Nash equilibrium with $7$ goods is EF1, so the $8$-good counterexample of arXiv:2610.23686 is the smallest possible, and $2n + 2$ is the exact threshold for three agents. For $n \ge 4$ it is open whether some instance with $2n + 2$ goods has a non-EF1 equilibrium; the threshold is at least $2n + 2$.

Several questions remain open:

- The exact threshold for $n \ge 4$: does the three-agent counterexample extend to $n$ agents and $2n + 2$ goods?
- The guaranteed factor: arXiv:2610.23686 leaves the gap $1/2 \le \alpha \le 2/3$ for the EF1 factor guaranteed at every equilibrium. The argument here suggests asking how the guaranteed factor depends on the number of goods per agent, not only on the number of agents.
- Alternative picking sequences: the results here concern the standard Round-Robin order. Other recursively balanced sequences may have different thresholds.
preliminaries:
Let us define the formal setting and concepts used in the theorems, matching the Lean 4 structures and definitions.

We consider a finite set of agents $N$ of cardinality $n \ge 1$ and a finite set of indivisible goods $G$ of cardinality $m \ge 0$. In Lean, these are represented by the standard finite types Fin $n$ and Fin $m$.

Definition 1 (Valuations and Additive Valuations). An abstract valuation is formalized by the structure `SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.Valuation`, which consists of a value function assigning a real number to each agent and bundle pair. An additive valuation is formalized by `SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.AdditiveValuation`, defined by a weight function assigning a real weight to each agent-good pair. The bundle valuation is obtained via the lifting `SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.AdditiveValuation.toValuation`, which sets
$$
v_i(S) = \sum_{g \in S} w(i, g)
$$
for any agent $i \in N$ and bundle $S \subseteq G$. Throughout our analysis, valuations are assumed to be nonnegative, meaning $w(i, g) \ge 0$ for all $i \in N$ and $g \in G$.

Definition 2 (Envy-Freeness up to One Good). Given a valuation $v$ and an allocation $A : N \to \text{Finset } G$ that assigns subsets of goods to agents, the property of envy-freeness up to one good (EF1) is formalized by `SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.IsEF1`:
$$
\forall i, j \in N, \ i \ne j \implies (A_j \text{ is nonempty} \implies \exists g \in A_j, \ v_i(A_j \setminus \{g\}) \le v_i(A_i)).
$$
Remark on Lean definition: The definition in Lean includes the guard that $A_j$ is nonempty. If agent $j$ receives an empty bundle ($A_j = \emptyset$), no good can be removed, and agent $i$ cannot envy an empty bundle under nonnegative valuations ($v_i(\emptyset) = 0 \le v_i(A_i)$). The definition also employs a weak inequality ($\le$).

Definition 3 (Round-Robin Picking Sequence). The Round-Robin sequence for $n$ agents and $m$ goods is defined in Lean by `round_robin_sequence`. Given $n$ and $m$, `round_robin_sequence n m` produces a list of agent indices of length $m$, where the active agent at step $t \in \{0, \dots, m-1\}$ is given by $t \pmod n$. Agents pick in the fixed cyclic order:
$$
(0, 1, \dots, n-1, 0, 1, \dots, n-1, 0, \dots).
$$

Definition 4 (Picking-Sequence Outcome). An agent's strategy is a reported strict ranking over the set of goods, formalized as a permutation of the goods, where position $0$ represents the agent's most preferred item and position $m-1$ their least preferred item. Given a sequence of agent turns and a profile of reported rankings, the mechanism `picking_sequence_outcome` determines the allocation $A : N \to \text{Finset } G$. The mechanism iterates through the turn sequence from left to right; at each step, the active agent takes the highest-ranked good in their reported ranking that has not yet been selected by any agent in an earlier step.

Definition 5 (Pure Nash Equilibrium of Picking Sequences). A profile of reported strict rankings is a pure Nash equilibrium (PNE) of the picking-sequence game, formalized by `is_picking_sequence_pne`, if no agent can achieve a bundle of strictly greater true value by unilaterally reporting an alternative ranking:
$$
\forall i \in N, \ \forall r, \ v_i(\text{picking\_sequence\_outcome } \text{seq } (\text{rank}[i \mapsto r])(i)) \le v_i(\text{picking\_sequence\_outcome } \text{seq } \text{rank}(i)).
$$
Remark on Lean definition: The equilibrium condition requires that any unilateral deviation produces an outcome whose true valuation is weakly less than or equal to the equilibrium outcome valuation. This is the standard definition of pure Nash equilibrium for normal-form games.

references.title: Revisiting the Fairness of Pure Nash Equilibria of Round-Robin

research: Proves exact EF1 for every number of agents when m <= 2n+1, a positive guarantee beyond the general 1/2-EF1 bound and the three-agent/eight-good counterexample in arXiv:2610.23686
tier_why: A general positive guarantee (every n, m <= 2n+1) by a short deviation argument, but not a question the paper poses; tightness is proved only for n = 3 (the paper's own 8-good example), the n >= 4 threshold is open, and the paper's central 1/2 vs 2/3 gap is untouched.

zh.title: 至多 $2n+1$ 个物品时循环机制的每个纯纳什均衡都满足至多一个物品的无嫉妒
zh.abstract: 在可加估值下的不可分物品公平分配中，当智能体诚实行动时，循环机制保证满足至多一个物品的无嫉妒（EF1）。然而，策略性智能体会通过报告偏好排序来最大化其所分配物品包的价值。在 arXiv:2610.23686 中已确立，虽然对于两个智能体，循环机制的每个纯纳什均衡（PNE）都是 EF1 的，但在一般情况下均衡可能不满足 EF1：该论文给出了一个包含三个智能体和八个物品的反例，并证明了一般的 $1/2$-EF1 近似界。该反例使用了 $m = 2n + 2$ 个物品；而对于任意数量的智能体，物品少至多少即可保证 EF1 在该文中并未讨论。我们证明了对于任意数量的智能体 $n \ge 1$ 以及任意数量的物品 $m \le 2n + 1$，非负可加估值下循环机制的每个纯纳什均衡都是 EF1 的。证明通过轮数分解分析：当 $m \le 2n$ 时，每个智能体至多选择两次，且均衡条件阻止了嫉妒程度超过一个物品；当 $m = 2n + 1$ 时，只有智能体 $0$ 分得三个物品，而所有其他智能体至多分得两个物品，且一个与估值无关的偏离论证表明，一旦移除智能体 $0$ 最初挑选的物品，所有其他智能体对智能体 $0$ 都是 EF1 的。对于三个智能体，该界是紧的：该论文中的八物品反例是最小的可能反例。这些结果已在 Lean 4 中形式化并验证。
zh.introduction:
在具有可加估值的智能体之间公平分配不可分物品的问题，是社会选择理论与算法博弈论中的基础课题。在为此设计的机制中，循环协议因其操作简便以及在真实行为下的优良公平性质而受到广泛研究。在循环协议中，智能体按循环次序轮流选择——智能体 $0$，接着是智能体 $1$，直至智能体 $n-1$，并循环往复——每个人从包含 $m$ 个物品的公共池中挑选自己最偏好的可用物品。循环协议的一个众所周知的经典性质是，当智能体报告其真实估值并近视地挑选时，所得到的分配保证满足至多一个物品的无嫉妒（EF1）：从被嫉妒的物品包中移除某个物品后，没有任何智能体嫉妒另一个智能体的物品包。

然而，在现实的分散式场景中，通常不能假定智能体会诚实行事。当智能体了解彼此的偏好时，他们可能会策略性地报告物品排序，而不是报告真实的序数偏好。报告的严格排序配置文件决定了选择序列的结果：每个智能体在轮到自己时，都会分得剩余物品中在其报告排序中排名最高的物品。这导出了一个范式博弈，即选择序列博弈，其中智能体的策略是其报告的物品排列。如果没有任何智能体能够通过单方面偏离到另一个不同的报告排序来获得具有严格更大真实可加价值的物品包，则报告排序的配置文件构成一个纯纳什均衡（PNE）。

策略性行为是否能保持循环机制的公平性保证，在 arXiv:2610.23686 中得到了研究。该论文表明，策略性相互作用确实会降低公平性。虽然该论文证明了对于 $n = 2$ 个智能体，循环机制的每个纯纳什均衡都会产生一个满足 EF1 的分配，但同样的保证并不能无条件地推广到三个或更多智能体的情形。具体而言，arXiv:2610.23686 在命题 1 中给出了一个包含 $n = 3$ 个智能体和 $m = 8$ 个物品的明确反例，其中某个纯纳什均衡不满足 EF1。在积极的一面，arXiv:2610.23686 证明了对于任意数量的智能体和物品，循环机制的每个纯纳什均衡都满足 $1/2$-EF1 近似界。

arXiv:2610.23686 的反例对 $3$ 个智能体使用了 $8$ 个物品，即在 $n = 3$ 时满足 $m = 2n + 2$。这引发了一个关于物品数量作用的自然问题：对于 $n$ 个智能体，物品数量最多达到多少时，循环机制的每个纯纳什均衡都保证满足 EF1？当 $m \le n$ 时，每个智能体至多挑选一次，EF1 是显然成立的；问题在于一旦智能体挑选多次会发生什么。

在本博文中，我们通过 Lean 4 形式化证明了：对于任意 $n \ge 1$ 以及任意 $m \le 2n + 1$，非负可加估值下循环机制的每个纯纳什均衡都是 EF1 的（`round_robin_pne_ef1_of_card_le_two_mul_add_one`）。这是对一个包含无限多个实例族的积极保证，涵盖了任意数量的智能体。

对于 $n = 3$，该界是紧的：在 $7$ 个物品时每个均衡都是 EF1 的，而论文中具有 $8$ 个物品的实例存在一个非 EF1 均衡。因此，arXiv:2610.23686 中的 $8$ 物品反例对于三个智能体而言是最小的可能反例。对于每个 $n \ge 4$ 是否 $2n + 2$ 个物品就足以打破 EF1，在此尚未得到证明，仍是一个公开问题。
zh.preliminaries:
我们定义定理中使用的形式化背景和概念，与 Lean 4 的结构和定义保持一致。

我们考虑基数为 $n \ge 1$ 的智能体有限集 $N$，以及基数为 $m \ge 0$ 的不可分物品有限集 $G$。在 Lean 中，它们分别由标准有限类型 Fin $n$ 和 Fin $m$ 表示。

定义 1（估值与可加估值）。抽象估值由结构体 `SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.Valuation` 形式化，它由一个为每个“智能体-物品包”对指定一个实数的价值函数组成。可加估值由 `SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.AdditiveValuation` 形式化，由一个为每个“智能体-物品”对指定一个实数权重的权重函数定义。物品包的估值通过提升映射 `SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.AdditiveValuation.toValuation` 获得，对于任意智能体 $i \in N$ 和物品包 $S \subseteq G$，它设定
$$
v_i(S) = \sum_{g \in S} w(i, g)
$$
在我们的整个分析中，假定估值是非负的，即对所有 $i \in N$ 和 $g \in G$，均有 $w(i, g) \ge 0$。

定义 2（至多一个物品的无嫉妒）。给定估值 $v$ 和将物品子集分配给智能体的分配 $A : N \to \text{Finset } G$，至多一个物品的无嫉妒（EF1）性质由 `SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.IsEF1` 形式化：
$$
\forall i, j \in N, \ i \ne j \implies (A_j \text{ is nonempty} \implies \exists g \in A_j, \ v_i(A_j \setminus \{g\}) \le v_i(A_i)).
$$
关于 Lean 定义的说明：Lean 中的定义包含了 $A_j$ 非空的守卫条件。如果智能体 $j$ 分得空物品包（$A_j = \emptyset$），则无法移除任何物品，而在非负估值下智能体 $i$ 不会嫉妒空物品包（$v_i(\emptyset) = 0 \le v_i(A_i)$）。该定义还采用了弱不等式（$\le$）。

定义 3（循环选择序列）。包含 $n$ 个智能体和 $m$ 个物品的循环序列在 Lean 中由 `round_robin_sequence` 定义。给定 $n$ 和 $m$，`round_robin_sequence n m` 会生成一个长度为 $m$ 的智能体索引列表，其中在步骤 $t \in \{0, \dots, m-1\}$ 处于行动轮次的智能体由 $t \pmod n$ 给出。智能体按固定的循环次序挑选：
$$
(0, 1, \dots, n-1, 0, 1, \dots, n-1, 0, \dots).
$$

定义 4（选择序列结果）。智能体的策略是关于物品集合的报告严格排序，形式化为物品的排列，其中位置 $0$ 表示该智能体最偏好的物品，位置 $m-1$ 表示其最不偏好的物品。给定智能体轮次序列和报告排序的配置文件，机制 `picking_sequence_outcome` 决定了分配 $A : N \to \text{Finset } G$。该机制从左到右遍历轮次序列；在每一步中，处于行动轮次的智能体从尚未被任何智能体在先前步骤中挑选的物品中，选择在其报告排序中排名最高的物品。

定义 5（选择序列的纯纳什均衡）。如果没有任何智能体可以通过单方面报告替代排序来获得具有严格更大真实价值的物品包，则报告严格排序的配置文件是选择序列博弈的纯纳什均衡（PNE），由 `is_picking_sequence_pne` 形式化：
$$
\forall i \in N, \ \forall r, \ v_i(\text{picking\_sequence\_outcome } \text{seq } (\text{rank}[i \mapsto r])(i)) \le v_i(\text{picking\_sequence\_outcome } \text{seq } \text{rank}(i)).
$$
关于 Lean 定义的说明：均衡条件要求任何单方面偏离所产生结果的真实估值都弱小于或等于均衡结果的估值。这是范式博弈中纯纳什均衡的标准定义。
zh.result:
在 Lean 4 中形式化的主要结果是：只要物品数量不超过 $2n + 1$，循环机制的每个纯纳什均衡都是 EF1 的。

定理（`round_robin_pne_ef1_of_card_le_two_mul_add_one`）。设 $n, m \in \mathbb{N}$，满足 $n \ge 1$ 且 $m \le 2n + 1$。设 $w : \text{Fin } n \to \text{Fin } m \to \mathbb{R}$ 为满足对所有 $i \in \text{Fin } n$ 和 $g \in \text{Fin } m$ 均有 $w(i, g) \ge 0$ 的权重矩阵，并诱导出可加估值 $v = \text{toValuation}(\langle w \rangle)$。设 $\text{rank} : \text{Fin } n \to (\text{Fin } m \simeq \text{Fin } m)$ 为报告排序的配置文件，它构成了长度为 $m$ 的循环序列的选择序列博弈的纯纳什均衡：
$$
\text{is\_picking\_sequence\_pne } v \ (\text{round\_robin\_sequence } n \ m) \ \text{rank}.
$$
那么该选择序列所得的分配满足至多一个物品的无嫉妒：
$$
\text{SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.IsEF1 } v \ (\text{picking\_sequence\_outcome } (\text{round\_robin\_sequence } n \ m) \ \text{rank}).
$$

在 Lean 中，`round_robin_pne_ef1_of_card_le_two_mul_add_one` 对自然数 $n$ 和 $m$ 进行了全称量化，并带有断言 $n$ 非零的类型类实例、不等式假设 $m \le 2n + 1$、带有非负性假设的物品权重矩阵 $w$、报告排序置换的配置文件以及纯纳什均衡假设，得出选择序列结果满足 `SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.IsEF1` 的结论。

形式化开发中的进一步结果为均衡的结构以及该界的锐度提供了额外的见解：

- `round_robin_pne_ef1_of_card_le_two_mul`: Proves that when $m \le 2n$, every pure Nash equilibrium of Round-Robin is EF1 under nonnegative additive valuations. In this regime, every agent appears at most twice in the picking sequence.
- `round_robin_pne_envy_zero_ef1_of_two_mul_add_one`: Establishes that when $m = 2n + 1$, in every pure Nash equilibrium, every agent $i \ne 0$ is EF1 towards agent $0$. Here, agent $0$ is the unique agent who receives three goods, while all other agents receive at most two.
- `round_robin_pne_ef1_pair_of_count_le_two`: Demonstrates that in any pure Nash equilibrium of Round-Robin, an agent $i$ is EF1 towards any agent $j$ who appears at most twice in the sequence.
- `round_robin_three_agents_seven_goods_pne_ef1`: Proves that for $n = 3$ agents and $m = 7$ goods, every pure Nash equilibrium of Round-Robin is EF1. This shows that the $8$-good counterexample of arXiv:2610.23686 is minimal: seven goods are never sufficient to break EF1.
zh.proof:
我们现在给出在 Lean 中形式化的 `round_robin_pne_ef1_of_card_le_two_mul_add_one` 的证明。

证明概述：

我们首先概述证明思路，然后陈述证明所依赖的引理，最后将它们结合以确立该定理。分析根据物品数量 $m$ 分为两种情形。

在 $m \le 2n$ 的情形下，物品总数至多是智能体数量的两倍。在循环序列中，每个智能体至多轮到两次。当一个智能体至多挑选两个物品时，均衡激励机制会阻止任何其他智能体对该智能体的嫉妒超过一个物品。这种情形由 `round_robin_pne_ef1_of_card_le_two_mul` 解决。

在 $m = 2n + 1$ 的情形下，恰好有一个智能体——智能体 $0$——挑选三个物品（在轮次 $0$、$n$ 和 $2n$）。所有其他智能体 $j \in \{1, \dots, n-1\}$ 至多挑选两个物品（具体在轮次 $j$ 和 $n + j$）。为验证整个分配的 EF1，我们考虑任意一对不同的智能体 $i$ 和 $j$：

- 如果被嫉妒的智能体 $j$ 满足 $j \ne 0$，那么 $j$ 在序列中至多挑选两次。由 `round_robin_pne_ef1_pair_of_count_le_two` 可知，智能体 $i$ 对 $j$ 的嫉妒不会超过一个物品。
- 如果被嫉妒的智能体 $j$ 是智能体 $0$（$j = 0$），那么 $j$ 挑选三个物品。然而，由于 $i \ne j$，我们有 $i \ne 0$。专用引理 `round_robin_pne_envy_zero_ef1_of_two_mul_add_one` 确立了任何智能体 $i \ne 0$ 对智能体 $0$ 都是 EF1 的。

将这些情形结合起来便覆盖了所有可能的配对，并确立了完整分配的 EF1。

我们现在陈述在形式化中确立并用于主定理的支持引理。

引理 1（`round_robin_pne_ef1_of_card_le_two_mul`）。
设 $n, m \in \mathbb{N}$，满足 $n \ge 1$ 且 $m \le 2n$。设 $w : \text{Fin } n \to \text{Fin } m \to \mathbb{R}$ 对所有 $i, g$ 满足 $w(i, g) \ge 0$，并设 $\text{rank}$ 为在由 $w$ 诱导的可加估值下循环机制的纯纳什均衡。那么 `picking_sequence_outcome` 在 `round_robin_sequence` 上返回的分配是 EF1 的。

在 Lean 中的作用：该引理处理 $m \le 2n$ 的子情形。当每个智能体在序列中至多出现两次时，没有任何智能体能分得三个或更多物品。如果智能体 $i$ 在从 $A_j$ 中移除任何单个物品后仍嫉妒智能体 $j$，则智能体 $j$ 必然持有两个物品 $\{g_1, g_2\}$ 使得 $v_i(\{g_1\}) > v_i(A_i)$ 且 $v_i(\{g_2\}) > v_i(A_i)$。然而，如果智能体 $i$ 偏离，选择机制允许其在自己的行动轮次中确保获得这些高价值物品中的至少一个，这与均衡假设 `is_picking_sequence_pne` 矛盾。

引理 2（`round_robin_sequence_count_le_two_of_ne_zero`）。
设 $n \in \mathbb{N}$ 且 $n \ge 1$。在包含 $n$ 个智能体且长度为 $2n + 1$ 的循环序列中，每个满足 $j \ne 0$ 的智能体 $j$ 至多出现两次：
$$
(\text{round\_robin\_sequence } n \ (2n + 1)).\text{count } j \le 2.
$$

Lean 中的证明：该序列由索引 $t \in \{0, 1, \dots, 2n\}$ 组成，其中轮次 $t$ 分配给智能体 $t \pmod n$。智能体 $0$ 分得轮次 $t \in \{0, n, 2n\}$，共计 $3$ 轮。对于任意智能体 $j \in \{1, \dots, n-1\}$，分配给 $j$ 的轮次是满足 $t \equiv j \pmod n$ 的值 $t \in \{0, \dots, 2n\}$。这些恰好是 $t = j$ 和 $t = n + j$。下一个潜在轮次将是 $2n + j$；然而，因为 $j \ge 1$，我们有 $2n + j \ge 2n + 1$，超过了序列长度 $m = 2n + 1$。因此，智能体 $j$ 恰好出现两次，从而以 $2$ 为界。

引理 3（`round_robin_pne_ef1_pair_of_count_le_two`）。
设 $n, m \in \mathbb{N}$ 且 $n \ge 1$。设 $w$ 定义非负可加估值，并设 $\text{rank}$ 为循环机制的纯纳什均衡。对于任意不同的智能体 $i, j$，如果智能体 $j$ 在选择序列中至多出现两次，
$$
(\text{round\_robin\_sequence } n \ m).\text{count } j \le 2,
$$
且 $A_j$ 非空，则智能体 $i$ 对智能体 $j$ 是 EF1 的：
$$
\exists g \in A_j, \ v_i(A_j \setminus \{g\}) \le v_i(A_i).
$$

Lean 中的证明：由于 $j$ 在序列中至多出现两次，物品包 $A_j$ 至多包含两个物品：$|A_j| \le 2$。若 $|A_j| = 1$，设 $A_j = \{g\}$。移除 $g$ 后留下空集 $A_j \setminus \{g\} = \emptyset$。在非负权重（$w \ge 0$）下，$v_i(\emptyset) = 0 \le v_i(A_i)$, 立即满足 EF1 条件。若 $|A_j| = 2$，设 $A_j = \{g_1, g_2\}$。不失一般性，假定 $w(i, g_1) \ge w(i, g_2)$。选择 $g = g_1$ 进行移除，我们有 $A_j \setminus \{g_1\} = \{g_2\}$，且 EF1 条件要求 $v_i(\{g_2\}) \le v_i(A_i)$。如果该条件不满足，则 $w(i, g_2) > v_i(A_i)$，进而 $w(i, g_1) \ge w(i, g_2) > v_i(A_i)$。这意味着 $A_j$ 中的两个物品单独对智能体 $i$ 产生的价值，都严格大于智能体 $i$ 均衡物品包 $A_i$ 的全部价值。在选择序列机制下，这两个物品中的至少一个在智能体 $i$ 的某个选择轮次中是可用的。智能体 $i$ 可以单方面改变其报告排序，将该物品置于其排序首位，从而确保获得一个价值严格大于 $v_i(A_i)$ 的物品，从而严格提高其总物品包价值。这与纯纳什均衡条件 `is_picking_sequence_pne` 矛盾。因此，$v_i(\{g_2\}) \le v_i(A_i)$，证明了智能体对 $(i, j)$ 满足 EF1。

引理 4（`round_robin_pne_envy_zero_ef1_of_two_mul_add_one`）。
设 $n \in \mathbb{N}$ 且 $n \ge 1$。在包含 $n$ 个智能体和 $2n + 1$ 个物品的循环序列中，在非负可加估值下，在每个纯纳什均衡 $\text{rank}$ 中，每个智能体 $i \ne 0$ 对智能体 $0$ 都是 EF1 的：
$$
\exists g \in A_0, \ v_i(A_0 \setminus \{g\}) \le v_i(A_i),
$$
其中 $A_k = \text{picking\_sequence\_outcome } (\text{round\_robin\_sequence } n \ (2n+1)) \ \text{rank } k$。

Lean 中的证明：当 $m = 2n + 1$ 时，智能体 $0$ 在轮次 $0$、$n$ 和 $2n$ 挑选；记其挑选的物品为 $a_1$、$a_2$、$a_3$，其中 $a_1$ 为其报告中排名最高的物品。智能体 $i \ne 0$ 在轮次 $i$ 和 $n + i$ 挑选并分得 $A_i = \{b_1, b_2\}$；注意 $0 < i < n < n + i < 2n$。从 $A_0$ 中移除的物品始终是 $a_1$，因此断言为 $w(i, a_2) + w(i, a_3) \le v_i(A_i)$。

证明首先确立了关于该机制的一个纯组合学事实，与估值无关：对于任何报告，要么 (a) 仅智能体 $i$ 的某个报告 $r$ 就使智能体 $i$ 获得同时包含 $a_2$ 和 $a_3$ 的物品包，要么 (b) 智能体 $i$ 的两个报告 $r_1$、$r_2$ 分别给出物品包 $D_1$、$D_2$，它们按重数共同覆盖 $A_i$ 和 $\{a_2, a_3\}$：每个物品在 $D_1$ 和 $D_2$ 中被计数的次数至少与在 $A_i$ 和 $\{a_2, a_3\}$ 中一样多。这是通过跟踪机制在智能体 $i$ 的最初挑选与智能体 $0$ 的最后挑选之间的轮次窗口中的运行，比较智能体 $i$ 提前拿走 $a_2$ 或 $a_3$ 时哪些物品仍可用而证明的。

然后由均衡条件完成论证。在情形 (a) 中，利用非负权重以及 $r$ 不是有利偏离的事实，有 $w(i, a_2) + w(i, a_3) \le v_i(\text{bundle under } r) \le v_i(A_i)$。在情形 (b) 中，覆盖关系给出 $v_i(A_i) + w(i, a_2) + w(i, a_3) \le v_i(D_1) + v_i(D_2) \le 2 v_i(A_i)$，同样由非负性以及对 $r_1$ 和 $r_2$ 应用均衡条件得出，因此 $w(i, a_2) + w(i, a_3) \le v_i(A_i)$。

结合各引理证明主定理：

我们现在追踪 `round_robin_pne_ef1_of_card_le_two_mul_add_one` 的 Lean 证明过程：

证明首先对不等式 $m \le 2n$ 进行分支。在 $m \le 2n$ 成立的分支中，证明直接应用 `round_robin_pne_ef1_of_card_le_two_mul`，从而立即完成目标。

在 $m \le 2n$ 不成立的分支中，我们有 $m > 2n$。结合假设 $m \le 2n + 1$，Lean 的算术策略确立了确切的等式 $m = 2n + 1$。证明将 $m$ 替换为 $2n + 1$。

为了证明 `SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.IsEF1`，证明引入了任意智能体 $i, j$、相异性假设 $i \ne j$ 以及 $A_j$ 非空的假设。

证明随后对 $j = 0$ 是否成立进行分支。当 $j = 0$ 时，代入 $j = 0$ 剩下展示智能体 $i$ 对智能体 $0$ 是 EF1 的目标。由于 $i \ne j$ 且 $j = 0$，我们有 $i \ne 0$。证明调用了引理 4，即 `round_robin_pne_envy_zero_ef1_of_two_mul_add_one`，该引理给出了所需的物品 $g \in A_0$。当 $j \ne 0$ 时，智能体 $j$ 不是智能体 $0$。证明应用了引理 2，即 `round_robin_sequence_count_le_two_of_ne_zero`，确认智能体 $j$ 在序列中至多出现两次。有了该计数界以及非空假设，证明调用了引理 3，即 `round_robin_pne_ef1_pair_of_count_le_two`，该引理给出了所需的物品 $g \in A_j$。

由于两种子情形都提供了一个在移除后可消除嫉妒的物品，因此该分配满足 EF1 条件。Lean 证明至此完整且完全通过验证。
zh.discussion:
结果 `round_robin_pne_ef1_of_card_le_two_mul_add_one` 为策略性循环机制的公平性提供了一个积极保证：只要物品数量满足 $m \le 2n + 1$，每个纯纳什均衡都是 EF1 的。这针对任意数量的智能体，将 arXiv:2610.23686 的双智能体 EF1 定理推广到了除智能体 $0$ 分得三个物品外、每个智能体至多分得两个物品的情形。

作为对比，arXiv:2610.23686 表明对于两个以上智能体，每个纯纳什均衡都是 $1/2$-EF1 的，精确的 EF1 可能会失效（命题 1，包含 $n = 3$ 个智能体和 $m = 8$ 个物品），并且通过一个智能体和物品数量递增的实例族，证明了无法保证高于 $2/3$ 的因子。

对于 $n = 3$，`round_robin_three_agents_seven_goods_pne_ef1`（主定理在 $n = 3$ 时的特例）表明具有 $7$ 个物品的每个纯纳什均衡都是 EF1 的，因此 arXiv:2610.23686 中的 $8$ 物品反例是最小的可能反例，且 $2n + 2$ 是三个智能体时的确切阈值。对于 $n \ge 4$，是否存在某个具有 $2n + 2$ 个物品的实例具有非 EF1 均衡仍是公开的；该阈值至少为 $2n + 2$。

仍有若干问题悬而未决：

- $n \ge 4$ 时的确切阈值：三智能体反例是否能推广到 $n$ 个智能体和 $2n + 2$ 个物品？
- 保证的因子：对于每个均衡所保证的 EF1 因子，arXiv:2610.23686 留下了 $1/2 \le \alpha \le 2/3$ 的差距。此处的论证提示人们去探究所保证的因子如何取决于每个智能体平均分得的物品数量，而不仅取决于智能体的数量。
- 替代选择序列：此处的结果涉及标准的循环次序。其他递归平衡的序列可能具有不同的阈值。
